key_impacts: Nearly 4.2 million cases and 284,000 deaths reported globally as of 11 May 2020.
COVID-19 epidemics can rapidly exceed healthcare capacity, including in high-income countries such as the US and Italy.

In many LICs/LMICs, the poorest households have limited access to handwashing facilities; in 22 of 26 countries assessed, less than 25% of households in the poorest quintile had soap and water at home.

Modeling estimates a 32.0% (2.5th–97.5th: 8.0%–72.5%) higher probability of death from COVID-19 in the poorest wealth quintile versus the wealthiest due to handwashing access, occupation, and hospital access.
The timing of the epidemic in low-resource settings has the potential to interrupt planting and harvesting seasons for staple crops, heightening food insecurity risks.
missing_information: Specific country-level impacts in LICs/LMICs are not enumerated.
Exact locations and dates where healthcare capacity was exceeded are not detailed.
Document does not quantify observed agricultural disruptions attributable to COVID-19 timing.
